Diane's 70th · Eurodam · Tuesday, August 31, 2027

Glacier Bay & Icy Strait Point

The best day of the trip. The morning is spent among tidewater glaciers in Glacier Bay National Park, then the evening at Icy Strait Point, beside Hoonah, Alaska's largest Tlingit village, with some of the best whale watching in the state.

Margerie Glacier · Yvrsigmatech, CC BY 2.0
6 am–3 pmGlacier Bay scenic cruising (no tours needed)
5:30 pmArrive at Icy Strait Point
~9:30 pmAll aboard (sails at 10 pm)
~8:15 pmSunset; good light until about 9
WhalesGuaranteed on the Point Adolphus whale tour

Morning · 6:00 am – 3:00 pm

Glacier Bay National Park

No excursions and no going ashore: the ship itself is the tour. National Park Service rangers board early near Bartlett Cove, narrate over the PA and in the lounges, help spot wildlife and run a mobile visitor center (bring your park passport for the stamp). A Huna Tlingit cultural interpreter shares the stories of their ancestral homeland. Everything is included in the fare.

  1. 6:00 amEnter the park. Rangers and the Tlingit interpreter come aboard.
  2. 7:30 amBalcony breakfast. Order room service the night before, and bundle up.
  3. Late morningTarr Inlet: Margerie and Grand Pacific glaciers, usually the turnaround. Expect about an hour in front of a calving tidewater glacier.
  4. MiddayDutch pea soup on the bow, a Holland America Glacier Bay tradition.
  5. Along the wayOften Johns Hopkins, Lamplugh and Reid glaciers. Watch for mountain goats, brown bears, sea otters and humpbacks.
  6. 3:00 pmLeave the park and sail to Icy Strait Point.

Our top three for Diane

If we only read one page

The Icy Strait Point call is a short evening, about 4½ hours ashore, so plan one 2–2½ hour tour or two short ones. These three are easy, memorable and fit the timing.

#1 · Best all-round

Whale Watch & Marine Mammal Safari

$219per person · ~2½ hrs

Point Adolphus is one of Alaska's richest humpback feeding grounds, often with sea lions and sometimes orcas, all in soft evening light.

Why for Diane: comfortable boat, whales guaranteed, and the same day as Glacier Bay.

Details & booking ↗
#2 · Bears

Spasski River Valley Wildlife & Bear Search

$134per person · ~2½ hrs

A short bus ride and level boardwalks to viewing platforms over a salmon stream. Late August is peak salmon, so bear odds are good.

Why for Diane: short walks on boardwalks and a real chance at brown bears.

Details & booking ↗
#3 · Gentle & fun

Sky Peak Gondola: Campfire & S'mores

$69per person · ~1½ hrs

Ride the gondola up Hoonah Mountain for big views, then gather around a campfire with s'mores as the light fades.

Why for Diane: easy, cozy and a sweet way to end a big day.

Details & booking ↗

On our own, for free (or close to it)

Icy Strait Point is a Native-owned destination, and its profits support Hoonah. The restored cannery and the trails are free to wander.

Icy Strait Point · Bernard Spragg, CC0
1912 cannery museum & shopsFree

The restored salmon cannery, with exhibits and local crafts.

Beach & forest trailsFree

Easy trails along the shore and into the rainforest.

Hoonah villageWalk or shuttle

About 1.5 miles to Alaska's largest Tlingit village.

Whales from shoreFree

Humpbacks are sometimes visible right from the shoreline.

Good to know

Before we book

Evening call. Not every tour runs on a 5:30–10 pm call, so confirm on the booking page.

Docking. Ships usually dock at Icy Strait Point's own pier rather than using tender boats. Check closer to sailing.

Glacier Bay route. Which glaciers we see depends on ice and wildlife on the day; Margerie and Grand Pacific are the usual turnaround.

Dress warmly. On deck in Glacier Bay it's often 45–50°F with wind. Bring a hat, gloves and binoculars.

Prices. Holland America refunds in full if it cancels a tour, and its Best Price Guarantee gives 110% of the difference as onboard credit if you find the identical tour cheaper.
